newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds start down after US, could stabilise.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds start down after US, could stabilise.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened lower on Friday echoing Wall Street declines and dealers predicted further falls ahead with possible stabilisation in later trade ahead of U.S. data.
"We're falling from the word go but things could well stabilise later up to the afternoon's U.S. February PPI and industrial data," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 opened down 0.24 point from Thursday's close at 110.66. The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 67 basis points. The crown opened at a slightly firmer 3.8153 per mark.
